ucs.title: [LLM] BlackByte BYOVD: RTCore64.sys driver-service install for kernel-mode EDR kill
ucs.description: Hunts BlackByte's signature Bring-Your-Own-Vulnerable-Driver chain — installation of the MSI Afterburner RTCore64.sys (or Dell DBUtil_2_3.sys) as a kernel service so the operator can disable AV/EDR from ring 0. This was the technique CrowdStrike & Sophos documented as BlackByte's defining defense-evasion move and is not how legitimate MSI Afterburner installs the driver (which uses its own installer, not sc.exe).
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND (Processes.process="*create*" OR Processes.process="*config*") AND (Processes.process="*RTCore64*" OR Processes.process="*rtcore64*" OR Processes.process="*DBUtil_2_3*" OR Processes.process="*DBUtil*" OR Processes.process="*RTC64*" OR Processes.process="*binPath=*RTCore*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="RTCore64.sys" OR Filesystem.file_name="DBUtil_2_3.sys") AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="*\\MSI Afterburner\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\MSI\\Afterburner\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Program Files\\Dell\\*") by Filesystem.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` ] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ScCreate = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "sc.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("create", "config")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("RTCore64", "rtcore64", "DBUtil_2_3", "DBUtil", "RTC64")    // RTCore64 = MSI Afterburner driver, DBUtil_2_3 = Dell BIOS driver — both abused by BlackByte for BYOVD
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal = "sc-create-vuln-driver";
let DriverDrop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("RTCore64.sys", "DBUtil_2_3.sys", "RTCore64.SYS")
    | where FolderPath !contains @"\MSI Afterburner\"
        and FolderPath !contains @"\Program Files\Dell\"
        and FolderPath !contains @"\drivers\"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              Signal = strcat("vuln-driver-drop:", FolderPath, "\\", FileName);
ScCreate
| union DriverDrop
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ScCreate = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\sc.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("create", "config")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("RTCore64", "rtcore64", "DBUtil_2_3", "DBUtil", "RTC64")    // BlackByte's BYOVD drivers — MSI Afterburner + Dell BIOS
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName,
              Signal = "sc-create-vuln-driver";
let DriverDrop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where TargetFileName in~ ("RTCore64.sys", "DBUtil_2_3.sys")
    | where TargetFilePath !contains @"\MSI Afterburner\"
        and TargetFilePath !contains @"\Program Files\Dell\"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, SubjectUserName = ActorUsername,
              CommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = ActingProcessName,
              Signal = strcat("vuln-driver-drop:", TargetFilePath);
ScCreate
| union DriverDrop
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: BlackByte BYOVD - RTCore64/DBUtil Vulnerable Driver Service Install
id: 7a4e9c1b-4b6d-4a9f-9c3d-2b6c5e1a8d11
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects sc.exe being used to create or configure a Windows service that
  references RTCore64.sys (MSI Afterburner) or DBUtil_2_3.sys (Dell BIOS) —
  both vulnerable drivers BlackByte ransomware abuses for kernel-mode AV/EDR
  termination (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver).
references:
  - https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/blackbyte-ransomware-uses-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-technique-to-disable-edr/
  - https://www.sophos.com/en-us/content/security-operations/blackbyte-toolkit
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/01/01
tags:
  - attack.defense-evasion
  - attack.privilege-escalation
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' create '
      - ' config '
  selection_driver:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'RTCore64'
      - 'rtcore64'
      - 'DBUtil_2_3'
      - 'DBUtil.sys'
      - 'RTC64'
  filter_legit:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\MSI Afterburner\'
      - '\Program Files\Dell\'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_driver and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Hardware-vendor installer dropping the driver from its official program-files path (covered by filter)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\sc.exe OR *\SC.exe OR *\SC.EXE) @CommandLine:(*RTCore64* OR *rtcore64* OR *DBUtil_2_3* OR *RTC64*) -@CommandLine:(*\MSI\ Afterburner\* OR *\Program\ Files\Dell\*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\sc\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)\\bcreate\\b|\\bconfig\\b", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(?i)RTCore64|rtcore64|DBUtil_2_3|RTC64", field=CommandLine)
| NOT regex("(?i)\\\\MSI Afterburner\\\\|\\\\Program Files\\\\Dell\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ucs.rationale: BlackByte is the canonical public example of BYOVD ransomware tradecraft — CrowdStrike, Sophos and Symantec all attribute the abuse of RTCore64.sys (and later DBUtil_2_3.sys) to this crew specifically, where the operator drops the signed-but-vulnerable Windows driver, registers it as a service via sc.exe, then writes a kernel IOCTL to terminate 1000+ AV/EDR process names from ring 0. ucs.title: [LLM] BlackByte exfil-then-wipe: Mega.io upload followed by VSS/bcdedit recovery destruction
ucs.description: Hunts BlackByte's characteristic dual-extortion sequence — outbound exfiltration to Mega cloud storage (via the actor's bespoke 'ExByte' Go uploader or rclone) followed within hours by shadow-copy deletion, bcdedit recovery-disable and wbadmin catalog destruction on the same host. The Mega.nz/io destination plus the wipe combo is the published BlackByte playbook (Symantec, Microsoft DEV-0382, CISA AA22-040A).
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as upload_first max(_time) as upload_last values(All_Traffic.app) as exfil_proc values(All_Traffic.dest) as mega_dest from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.url="*mega.nz*" OR All_Traffic.url="*mega.io*" OR All_Traffic.url="*mega.co.nz*" OR All_Traffic.url="*userstorage.mega.co.nz*" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.mega.nz" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.mega.io") AND NOT All_Traffic.app IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe") by All_Traffic.src | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | join type=inner src [| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as destruct_first max(_time) as destruct_last values(Processes.process) as recovery_cmds values(Processes.process_name) as recovery_tools from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("vssadmin.exe","wmic.exe","bcdedit.exe","wbadmin.exe","powershell.exe") AND (Processes.process="*delete shadows*" OR Processes.process="*shadowcopy*delete*" OR Processes.process="*recoveryenabled*No*" OR Processes.process="*ignoreallfailures*" OR Processes.process="*delete catalog*" OR Processes.process="*Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy*Delete*") by Processes.dest | rename Processes.dest as src | fields src recovery_cmds recovery_tools destruct_first destruct_last] | where destruct_first >= upload_first AND (destruct_first - upload_last) < 21600 | eval delay_minutes=round((destruct_first - upload_last)/60,1) | table src exfil_proc mega_dest upload_first upload_last destruct_first delay_minutes recovery_tools recovery_cmds | sort - upload_first
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowHours = 6h;    // empirical: BlackByte typically detonates ransomware within ~2-4h of last Mega upload
let MegaExfil = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("mega.nz", "mega.io", "mega.co.nz", "userstorage.mega.co.nz", "g.api.mega.co.nz")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","MegaSync.exe")    // exclude only sanctioned MegaSync — BlackByte renames bring their own
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | summarize UploadFirst = min(Timestamp), UploadLast = max(Timestamp),
                BytesProxy = count(),
                ExfilProcess = any(InitiatingProcessFileName),
                ExfilCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
                MegaHost = any(RemoteUrl)
                by DeviceName;
let RecoveryDestruction = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("shadows", "shadowstorage"))
        or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "shadowcopy" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete")
        or (FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("recoveryenabled no", "ignoreallfailures", "bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures"))
        or (FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("catalog", "systemstatebackup", "backup"))
        or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("Win32_Shadowcopy", "Delete"))
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | summarize DestructFirst = min(Timestamp), DestructLast = max(Timestamp),
                RecoveryTools = make_set(FileName),
                RecoveryCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 5)
                by DeviceName;
MegaExfil
| join kind=inner RecoveryDestruction on DeviceName
| where DestructFirst between (UploadFirst .. UploadLast + WindowHours)
| project UploadFirst, UploadLast, DestructFirst,
          DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', DestructFirst, UploadLast),
          DeviceName, ExfilProcess, ExfilCmd, MegaHost,
          RecoveryTools, RecoveryCmds
| order by UploadFirst desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowHours = 6h;
let MegaExfil = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("mega.nz", "mega.io", "mega.co.nz", "userstorage.mega")
         or DestinationHostName has_any ("mega.nz", "mega.io", "mega.co.nz")
    | where SourceUserName !endswith "$"
    | summarize UploadFirst = min(TimeGenerated), UploadLast = max(TimeGenerated),
                Hits = count(), MegaHost = any(coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName)),
                ExfilProcess = any(DestinationProcessName)
                by Computer = SourceHostName;
let RecoveryDestruction = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\vssadmin.exe" and CommandLine has "delete" and CommandLine has_any ("shadows", "shadowstorage"))
        or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "shadowcopy" and CommandLine has "delete")
        or (NewProcessName endswith "\\bcdedit.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("recoveryenabled no", "ignoreallfailures"))
        or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wbadmin.exe" and CommandLine has "delete" and CommandLine has_any ("catalog","systemstatebackup"))
        or (NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has_all ("Win32_Shadowcopy","Delete"))
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | summarize DestructFirst = min(TimeGenerated), DestructLast = max(TimeGenerated),
                RecoveryTools = make_set(NewProcessName),
                RecoveryCmds = make_set(CommandLine, 5)
                by Computer;
MegaExfil
| join kind=inner RecoveryDestruction on Computer
| where DestructFirst between (UploadFirst .. UploadLast + WindowHours)
| project UploadFirst, UploadLast, DestructFirst,
          DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', DestructFirst, UploadLast),
          Computer, ExfilProcess, MegaHost, RecoveryTools, RecoveryCmds
| order by UploadFirst desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*mega.nz OR *mega.io OR *mega.co.nz OR *userstorage.mega.co.nz) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\brave.exe OR *\opera.exe OR *\iexplore.exe OR *\MegaSync.exe OR *\MEGAsync.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(^|\.)mega\.(nz|io|co\.nz)$/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|MegaSync|MEGAsync)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count(as=req_count))
| req_count > 5
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | regex("(?i)\\\\(vssadmin|wmic|bcdedit|wbadmin)\\.exe$", field=ImageFileName) | regex("(?i)delete shadows|shadowcopy.*delete|recoveryenabled No|ignoreallfailures|delete catalog", field=CommandLine)}, field=aid, include=[ImageFileName, CommandLine])
ucs.rationale: BlackByte is one of a small handful of crews that consistently exfiltrate to Mega cloud storage via their bespoke Go uploader ExByte (Symantec named it after observing the binary string 'ExByte' in actor C2) and then immediately destroy local recovery before encrypting — Microsoft and CISA called this combo out by name in DEV-0382 / AA22-040A. Mega.nz traffic alone or vssadmin delete shadows alone
